title: Site locality casebook and audit evidence template
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operator-friendly casebook for customer-specific locality requirements (aka data 'locality') and an evidence packaging template for audits. Intended for SREs, SEs, and privacy engineers who need a "one-page" decisioning aid and an example artifact bundle when customers request proof that traffic/storage remained within agreed jurisdictions.

Scope and intent:
- Focus: customer-level per-tenant locality constraints for Private + Dedicated deployments (region affinity, storage anchors, network egress controls).
- Not in scope: enterprise legal contract language (see legal team for final clauses). This doc shows pragmatic technical controls and the minimal audit artifacts to collect.

Quick decision matrix (high level):
- If customer requires "no egress outside jurisdiction": pin compute + store in region, enforce VPC-only egress, restrict third-party telemetry forwarding.
- If customer allows "controlled subprocessing": allow certified sub-processors in approved regions, require signed addendum and telemtry tags.
- If customer requests "logical separation only": enforce tenant isolation, limit operator access, and supply opaque audit evidence.

Sample customer scenarios (realistic, anonymized):
1) EU national telco (high assurance)
   - Requirement: All inference and user content storage must stay within EU; logs may only contain pseudonymous IDs; audit evidence for last 90 days.
   - Recommended enforcement: region_pin=eu-west-1 for both compute and store; storage class: regional-block; KMS keys scoped to EU; egress rules: deny any non-EU CIDR; disable external telemetry export for this tenant.
   - Evidence bundle example: infra-as-code plan (Terraform diff), route table dumps, KMS key metadata, sample request traces filtered by tenant-id, parity checksum of dataset snapshots with location timestamps.

2) APAC healthcare research org (regulated, limited share)
   - Requirement: Data residency in APAC (Singapore preferred), cross-border export allowed for model parameters only with DTA, 180-day retention minimum.
   - Recommended enforcement: deploy private control plane VPC in ap-sg-1, store PII in customer-managed S3 equivalent with lifecycle rules, enforce TTL and retention policy via lifecycle-policy-id in audit bundle.
   - Evidence bundle example: retention-policy.json, object-listing CSV with object creation time and region, consent form scan, Data Transfer Agreement id.

3) North American fintech (soft locality)
   - Requirement: Logical tenancy in NA; fallbacks to non-NA allowed but must be auditable and rate-limited.
   - Recommended enforcement: tenant affinity to na-central region, runtime tag telemetry: locality_hint=NA, fallback_policy: fallback_to_nearest_compatible with explicit sampling for cross-border calls at 0.1% and alerting on any non-zero rate change.
   - Evidence bundle example: sampled cross-border call log (0.1% sampling), sampling selector code snippet, alerting policy snapshot.

Operator runbook (when a customer raises compliance question):
- Step 0: Triage via support ticket and capture the required evidence scope (time window, artifact types). Create a Jira under INF-3128 if not already present.
- Step 1: Confirm current tenant config: show pinned region, storage anchors, KMS ARN, egress rules, and control-plane location (single command to generate JSON).
- Step 2: Pull traces: take last N requests (configurable, default 1M tokens or 7 days), filter by tenant-id, and run evidence extraction script (see code snippet below).
- Step 3: Assemble artifact bundle (zip) with README.md describing each file and signatures from SRE on checks performed. Store bundle in audit-bucket with retention 1 year, and share secure link with customer.
- Step 4: If any deviation found, escalate to privacy-eng + legal within 4 hours (page oncall), create an incident with mitigations (temporary customer isolation, rollback to snapshot, deny new tenant traffic).

Minimal evidence packaging template (what to include in every bundle):
- README.md (one paragraph summary, time window, contact)
- infra-diff.txt (Terraform diff or ARM plan)
- routing-snapshot.txt (route tables, peering attachments)
- storage-manifests.csv (object key, size, region, last-modified)
- policy-assertions.json (pinned_region, fallback_policy, retention_policy_id)
- sample-traces.log (redacted request traces with tenant-id, geo tags, timestamps)
- kms-keys.csv (key-id, region, owner)
- operator-signoff.txt (name, time, summary)

Practical extraction regex and example (operator-friendly):
- tenant filter: /tenant_id=(?<tenant>[a-z0-9-]+)/i
- geo tag: /locality_hint=(?<loc>[-_a-z0-9]+)/i
- sample trace excerpt: "ts=2024-11-17T14:03:22Z tenant_id=acct-9902 locality_hint=eu-west-1 action=generate tokens=42"

Audit heuristics (what auditors will look for):
- Chain of custody: presence of signed operator signoff and immutable timestamps.
- Determinism: infra-diff plus resource-id parity to show resources existed in cited region at time X.
- Telemetry sufficiency: a deterministic sampling policy or full traces with redaction.

Fallback and mitigation patterns (operator notes):
- Soft-fallback allowed: must be tied to explicit, time-limited policy and included in evidence as a fallback event with reason code.
- Hard-exception: only via legal-approved SLA amendment; requires offline approval and must be recorded in contract addendum id.

Templates for customer communication (short):
- Acknowledgement to customer: "Received request for locality evidence for tenant <id>. We'll return a signed artifact bundle within 3 business days; if you require a faster turnaround please escalate to your CSM."
- Escalation: "Immediate action: deviation found — temporarily isolated tenant and assigned incident INF-<number>. SRE and legal are engaged."

Open questions / TODOs (operate-as-code notes):
- Can we add automated bundle generation (lambda job) per customer with RBAC restricted download links? (low effort prototype: 2w)
- Decide canonical TTL for audit bundles (current suggestion: 1 year, legal may require longer per contract).
- Standardize redaction policy for traces (PII removal heuristics).
- Add end-to-end test that spins up a sample tenant pinned to each supported region and runs a verification harness weekly.

References and related artifacts:
- Confluence: Locality Design page (link in header)
- Jira: INF-3128 (locality evidence workstream)
- Example PR: git@github.com:redwood/repo-private-deploy-simulations#42 (simulation harness for telco scenario)

Notes to self (choppy):
- When in doubt, show resource ids + immutable timestamps — auditors like receipts.
- Keep examples short in README; auditors ask for full bundles but humans scan README first.
- For telco-level customers, expect follow-up on KMS key custody and HSM attestations.

Appendix: quick shell snippet to produce core artifacts (toy example):
- terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan && terraform show -no-color plan.tfplan > infra-diff.txt
- aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC > routing-snapshot.txt
- aws s3api list-objects --bucket $BUCKET --prefix tenant-$TENANT --query 'Contents[].[Key,Size,LastModified]' > storage-manifests.csv
- elasticsearch query: tenant_id:$TENANT AND @timestamp:[start TO end] | head 1000 > sample-traces.log

End of document.
